title: Provision Auto Scaling Group
scenario: Your platform team needs Auto Scaling Group for elastic capacity across subnets. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_autoscaling_group.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).

focus.title: Complete the aws_autoscaling_group resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_autoscaling_group.

hints.why: EC2 teaches the core lifecycle of compute: image, instance type, networking, storage and safe replacement.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_autoscaling_group. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use EC2 when you need a virtual machine you control directly, or as a building block inside an autoscaling or container platform.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "this"`. Use this code shape: name; min_size; max_size; desired_capacity; vpc_zone_identifier; launch_template { id; version }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.asg_min`, `var.asg_max`, `var.asg_desired`, `var.subnet_ids`, `aws_launch_template.this.id`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
